abstract_sentences.text: An agent must try new behaviors to explore and improve.

evidence.anchor: An agent must try new behaviors

abstract_sentences.text: In high-stakes environments, an agent that violates safety constraints may cause harm and must be taken offline, curtailing any future interaction.

evidence.anchor: violates safety constraints may cause harm

abstract_sentences.text: Imitating old behavior is safe, but excessive conservatism discourages exploration.
How much behavior change is too much?
abstract_sentences.transition: Converts the tension into a selection question.

evidence.anchor: How much behavior change is too much?

abstract_sentences.text: We show how to use any safe reference policy as a probabilistic regulator for any optimized but untested policy.
abstract_sentences.comparison_target: safe reference policy versus optimized policy

abstract_sentences.text: Conformal calibration on data from the safe policy determines how aggressively the new policy can act, while provably enforcing the user's declared risk tolerance.
Unlike conservative optimization methods, we do not assume the user has identified the correct model class nor tuned any hyperparameters.
abstract_sentences.transition: Positions against model-class and tuning assumptions.

abstract_sentences.text: Unlike previous conformal methods, our theory provides finite-sample guarantees even for non-monotonic bounded loss functions, and it introduces a new policy control setting.

Our experiments on applications ranging from natural language question answering to biomolecular engineering show that safe exploration is not only possible from the first moment of deployment, but can also improve performance.
abstract_sentences.comparison_target: natural language question answering to biomolecular engineering

abstract_summary.reported_result_type: Qualitative: safe exploration is possible from first deployment and can improve performance; no numerical value in the abstract.
abstract_summary.mentions_limitations: Only high-stakes harm and conservatism are named; safe-policy, absolute-continuity, stability, and context-shift requirements are absent from the abstract.
abstract_summary.strongest_claim_placement: The finite-sample guarantee occurs in sentence 8; cross-domain performance occurs in the final sentence.

introduction_moves.current_answer: Frames safe exploration as the explore-exploit and validity-power dilemma.
introduction_moves.next_hook: A general solution needs a problem-independent balance.

introduction_moves.prior_open_question: What does this balance mean for an agent?
introduction_moves.current_answer: Medical QA and biomolecular engineering instantiate reward, loss, safe defaults, and untested optimized policies.
introduction_moves.next_hook: Can safe-policy data select a candidate policy?

introduction_moves.prior_open_question: Why not choose the estimated-safe candidate?
introduction_moves.current_answer: Selection favors underestimated risks even when each candidate can be importance weighted.
introduction_moves.next_hook: Use the agent-known policy shift in calibration.

introduction_moves.prior_open_question: How can policy choice itself be calibrated?
introduction_moves.current_answer: CPC searches likelihood-ratio-parameterized candidate policies and deploys the selected one by rejection sampling.
introduction_moves.next_hook: Why finite-sample control survives this data-dependent policy choice.

introduction_moves.prior_open_question: Why standard CRC cannot directly cover CPC.
introduction_moves.current_answer: The control parameter governs policy, so loss need not be monotone; gCRC handles non-monotonic bounded losses.

formal_objects.input: Contexts X, actions A, rewards r/R, losses ℓ/L, safe policy π0, optimized policy πt, calibration data, proposal data, target α, loss bound B.
formal_objects.output: A clipped constrained policy π_t^(β̂), deployed by accept–reject sampling.
formal_objects.state: Sequential policy-improvement history; permutation/mixture conformal weights encode prior-policy data.
formal_objects.objective: Maximize expected reward subject to expected loss at most α in Eq. (1).

result_inventory.claim: gCRC controls MedLFQA FDR at or below the target alpha while retaining recall at least as high, often higher, than baselines.
result_inventory.value: Figure 4 curves; no cell-wise numeric table. Results are averaged over 25 random splits with standard-error regions.
result_inventory.comparison: gCRC versus LTT and monotonized-loss CRC.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Mean over 25 independent random splits; FDR and recall; standard errors. No test, p-value, bootstrap, Bayesian analysis, or multiple-comparison correction reported.
result_inventory.author_interpretation: LTT is described as conservative due to high-probability concentration inequalities; monotonized-loss CRC is described as conservative due to Jensen’s inequality.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: The result is based on MedLFQA and an LLM annotation pipeline; Figure 10 broadens scoring methods but not the application domain.

result_inventory.claim: CPC controls active-learning constraint violation at alpha=0.2 and in some cases lowers test MSE.
result_inventory.value: Figure 5 has trajectories for Robot Arm Kinematics, Airfoil, and MEPS; exact per-step values are not tabulated.
result_inventory.comparison: CPC versus Uncontrolled and Conformal Controller.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Trajectory plots; seed count, aggregation denominator, ribbon interpretation, and hypothesis testing are not_present.
result_inventory.author_interpretation: Avoiding infeasible regions improves sample efficiency.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: The feasibility constraint is synthetic and PCA-based; the mechanism is not isolated with a component ablation.

result_inventory.claim: In Ehrlich sequence optimization, CPC controls infeasibility while preserving objective improvement; moderate alpha above 0.6 can slightly outperform the uncontrolled counterpart.

result_inventory.adverse_explanation: Ehrlich is a procedural synthetic benchmark; no real biomolecular assay is evaluated.

final_judgment.single_storyline: CPC turns self-authored distribution shift into a likelihood-ratio-clipped policy family, calibrates the family directly on safe-policy data to a user-declared alpha, then deploys the selected beta by rejection sampling. [pp.1–3, 6–7]
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The selection-bias problem, Figure 1 pipeline, Eq. (5)–(6), two main guarantee statements, Algorithm 1, Figures 4–6, and marginal/context/likelihood boundaries. [pp.2, 5–9]
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proofs, normalizer and mixture-weight approximation, sampling, dataset construction, hyperparameters, extra score robustness, and CBO comparison move to pp.16–53. Reproduction and appraisal of the practical approximation require D.1.3. [pp.40–43]
final_judgment.best_pattern: A full-width process diagram precedes formulas; beta interpolation visualization, theorem statements, and task figures then close mechanism, guarantee, and evidence in the same order. [pp.2, 5–9]
final_judgment.largest_gap: The exact-weight theorem and the mixture/empirical-wmax implementation are separated without a stated finite-sample approximation theorem; non-Medical-QA aggregation and ribbon semantics are also missing, and Figure 5 conflicts with Table 3 on iteration count. [pp.7, 41–43, 51]
final_judgment.transfer_rule: Map a user-legible target risk to a system-owned, calibratable policy family, so candidate selection is itself the calibrated act rather than an uncalibrated step after evaluation.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The rule needs a trusted safe baseline, bounded loss, mutual absolute continuity, likelihood availability or a justified approximation, calibration stability, and sufficiently stable context distribution. [pp.6–7, 9, 40–43]
